blocks.text: Condo buildings in Port Kells

Filing position — stated openly at the top. Geography trap, stated here: Barnston Island is NOT in Surrey — it is Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A plus Katzie IR 3; it codes to Port Kells for board purposes only because the Barnston Island Ferry lands at the foot of 104 Avenue in Port Kells. Surrey's current OCP is Surrey 2050, Bylaw No. 21900 (adopted June 15, 2026) — the former Bylaw No. 18020 is never cited as current. The 55+ program found zero seniors housing of any type in-area.
Streets, schools and getting around Port Kells

items.t: Port Kells sits in the northeast corner of Surrey, on the south bank of the Fraser River, north and south of Highway 1, east of Highway 15 (176 Street), against the Langley border. It has two distinct halves: a large light-industrial district north of Highway 1, and a rural/low-density residential pocket ("South Port Kells") south of the highway. The City's economic arm profiles Port Kells as one of Surrey's major industrial areas (781 acres, roughly 610 businesses, mainly light industrial IL zoning).

Nearby areas: Tynehead and Fleetwood (west/southwest), Guildford (west), Walnut Grove in the Township of Langley (east), Anniedale-Tynehead (immediately south, Neighbourhood Concept Plan in preparation).

Where condo stock concentrates: nowhere — there is no condo shelf. The residential stock is single-detached houses on suburban and larger rural lots plus cluster housing shown in the South Port Kells Land Use Plan, predominantly freehold; north of Highway 1 the land is industrial buildings, not housing.

Community (Surrey, all of Surrey) — detached median $1,215,000, $454/sq ft, 95% sale-to-list, 28 days on market; condos & townhomes median $512,944, $491/sq ft, 99% sale-to-list, 25 days on market. The sub-area sample is too small for its ratios to mean anything on their own.

Schools: Port Kells Elementary (K–7) at 19076 88 Avenue, School District 36 (Surrey); the current school building opened in 1907 and is on the Canadian Register of Historic Places. A locator run for 19076 88 Avenue returned Port Kells Elementary and Ecole Salish Secondary. Catchments are address-based — confirm other addresses in the locator.

Highway 1, Highway 15 (south to the U.S. commercial border crossing) and Highway 17 / South Fraser Way run through or beside the area. The Barnston Island Ferry (free, provincial inland ferry, roughly 5-minute on-demand crossing, capacity ~6 vehicles) departs from the foot of 104 Avenue across Parson's Channel.

Recreation and shopping: no civic recreation centre and no retail centre in Port Kells itself; Tynehead Regional Park (Metro Vancouver) borders the area to the west, and the nearest full shopping is in Guildford and Langley's Walnut Grove.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Port Kells

items.t: City plan and zoning: Surrey 2050 Official Community Plan, Bylaw No. 21900 (adopted June 15, 2026) is Surrey's current OCP — Bylaw No. 18020 is superseded and must not be cited as current. Area-level guidance is the adopted South Port Kells Land Use Plan; North Port Kells is primarily light industrial (IL) zoning. Surrey publishes Port Kells-specific Development Cost Charges (2025 Port Kells Industrial DCCs and Commercial DCCs, separate from city-wide rates) — a real line item for any industrial or commercial purchase with development intent.

ALR rules govern the south pocket's farm parcels: the South Port Kells plan maps ALR boundary lands through the residential pocket; ALR status changes what a buyer can build, and ALC housing rules generally allow one residence per parcel (principal residence 500 m² or less, secondary suite only inside the principal residence). Check the ALR boundary on any south-side parcel before pricing in a second dwelling.

Surrey suites rule: a secondary suite in Surrey is capped at 40% of the principal dwelling's habitable area — the suite rule that applies if a South Port Kells house (or any Surrey house a buyer chooses instead of a condo) is bought with suite income in mind; ALR parcels follow the ALC rule above instead. City of Surrey Zoning By-law No. 12000 suite provisions, as applied program-wide in this notes series.

blocks.text: Good to know about Port Kells

items.t: One name, two unrelated markets, split by a highway. North of Highway 1: an IL-zoned industrial district with its own DCC schedule and roughly 610 businesses. South of it: a rural-residential pocket under a separate adopted land use plan, with ALR parcels woven through it. A "Port Kells" search has to be split by highway side before it means anything.
The board stats will mislead if read at face value.
The island across the ferry is not in Surrey at all.

The school is a heritage building. Port Kells Elementary's current building opened in 1907 and is on the Canadian Register of Historic Places — the old village core around 88 Avenue is the residential pocket's historic centre, in a sub-area otherwise defined by warehouses.

Anniedale-Tynehead is the change to watch. The Neighbourhood Concept Plan in preparation directly south contemplates industrial, commercial and residential growth next to Port Kells — servicing, traffic and land values on the south edge move with that plan, not with anything happening inside Port Kells itself.
Surrey replaced its OCP in 2026. Surrey 2050, Bylaw No. 21900 (adopted June 15, 2026), is the current plan — packages and older guides citing Bylaw 18020 are citing a superseded bylaw.

The residential stock is single-detached houses on suburban and larger rural lots plus cluster housing shown in the South Port Kells Land Use Plan, predominantly freehold; north of Highway 1 the land is industrial buildings, not housing.

Schools (SD36; Ministry-listed names): Port Kells Elementary (K–7) at 19076 88 Ave serves the area; the current school building opened in 1907 and is on the Canadian Register of Historic Places. Catchments are address-based — that chain is settled for the test address only.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Port Kells

items.t: Form B diligence (any strata purchase — stated as the governing frame; there is no verified Port Kells strata to request one from today): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. It governs any strata purchase a buyer makes instead in Guildford/Fleetwood, and any future strata product here.

Fee-simple reality — stated plainly, because it is the local stock: A fee-simple home carries NO strata, NO Form B and NO strata fees; municipal rules (Surrey Zoning Bylaw No. 12000) plus any registered covenants or homeowners' association govern instead.

ALR frame — carried in full because the research documents ALR lands woven through the South Port Kells residential pocket: ALR residences cannot be stratified (ALC Bulletin 09 s. 6; Strata Property Act s. 239; Agricultural Land Commission Act s. ALC housing caps: a principal residence of 500 m² or less; a secondary suite only inside the principal residence; an additional residence of 90 m² or less on parcels of 40 ha or less, or 186 m² or less on parcels over 40 ha, under the ALC's rules or with approval. Check the ALR boundary on any south-side parcel before pricing in a second dwelling.

Secondary suites (Surrey, off-ALR parcels): one secondary suite may be permitted in a single family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling, capped at 40% of the principal dwelling unit's habitable floor area under Zoning Bylaw No. 12000, one per unit, not a separate strata lot, and never inside a coach house or garden suite. ALR parcels follow the ALC rule above instead.

faq.q: How many homes are for sale in Port Kells?

faq.q: How many homes sold in Port Kells from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 0 houses and 0 condos and townhomes sold in Port Kells over those 4 months.

faq.q: How big is Port Kells compared with the rest of Surrey?
faq.a: In September 2026, Port Kells held 0.4% of the 1,120 detached houses listed in Surrey.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Port Kells than in June?
faq.a: Listings of detached houses was 2 in June and 4 in September 2026, too few (under 3) to call a rise or fall.

faq.q: Is there a condo or townhome I can buy in Port Kells?
faq.a: No verified one. The board recorded 0 condos & townhomes listings in the sub-area in September 2026, and no named strata complex of any form verifies in-area on any source checked. A buyer set on strata product is shopping Guildford, Fleetwood or Walnut Grove, not Port Kells. SnapStats FVR September 2026 report.

faq.q: What CAN I buy in Port Kells?
faq.a: A freehold house in South Port Kells (suburban lots to multi-acre rural/ALR parcels) or, north of Highway 1, an industrial property. The two markets share a name and almost nothing else.

faq.q: Is Port Kells really a board sub-area, or just an industrial park name?
faq.a: Both things are true: it is a real FVREB sub-area in the board's SnapStats structure (Jared's ruling) AND the City profiles it as a major industrial area; it is not one of Surrey's six town centres.

faq.q: Is Barnston Island part of Port Kells / Surrey?
faq.a: No. Barnston Island is Metro Vancouver Electoral Area A plus Katzie IR 3 — it only codes to Port Kells for board purposes because the free ferry to it sails from the foot of 104 Avenue in Port Kells. Do not price or describe an island property as Surrey stock.

faq.q: Can I build a suite or second home on a South Port Kells acreage?
faq.a: It depends on zoning and, critically, ALR status: the land use plan shows ALR lands inside the residential pocket, and ALR parcels carry the ALC's residence limits (secondary suite only inside the principal residence). Off-ALR, Surrey's suite cap is 40% of the principal dwelling's habitable area. Confirm both before pricing in a second dwelling.

faq.q: Is there a townhouse I can buy in Port Kells?
faq.a: No verified one — of either tenure. The board recorded 0 condos & townhomes listings in the sub-area in September 2026, no named strata complex of any form verifies in-area on any source checked, and this pass's fresh check surfaced detached houses only. A buyer set on townhouse product is shopping Guildford, Fleetwood or Walnut Grove, not Port Kells.

faq.q: What CAN I buy in Port Kells?
faq.a: A freehold house in South Port Kells (suburban lots to multi-acre rural/ALR parcels) or, north of Highway 1, an industrial property. The two markets share a name and almost nothing else.

faq.q: Is Port Kells really a board sub-area, or just an industrial park name?
faq.a: Both things are true: it is a real FVREB sub-area in the board's SnapStats structure (Jared's ruling) AND the City profiles it as a major industrial area; it is not one of Surrey's six town centres, and for community planning it sits within the Guildford area's orbit.
